days.topic: What to Do First After Getting Engaged
days.hook: Stop. Before you book ANYTHING — do these 5 things.
days.caption:
Everyone told me to 'enjoy the moment' after getting engaged — and they were right. But before the planning spiral starts, there are 5 things you should do FIRST that'll save you months of stress. Watch this before you open a single vendor website. 💍

1. Tell your people before it's online
2. Take engagement photos ASAP
3. Set a rough budget range before venues
4. Agree on a guest count ballpark
5. Give yourself 2-4 weeks before booking anything

Which step surprised you most? Drop it below! 👇

days.topic: Guest List Strategy That Saves Money and Stress
days.hook: Every person you add to your guest list costs you $150-$250. Do the math.
days.caption:
Nobody wants to be the couple cutting names — but the guest list IS the budget. 💔

Here's the framework we use with every couple:

1. Start with your 'anytime list' (immediate family + closest friends)
2. Add your 'maybe list' and sit on it for a week
3. Apply the '2-year rule' — seen them in the last 2 years?

This approach alone helped one couple cut 40 guests and save $6k. 🙌

Drop your biggest guest list challenge below. We've seen it all. 👇
days.content_tip: Pair with relatable meme in Stories. High engagement topic — people ALWAYS have opinions on guest lists.

days.topic: How We Saved $3,000 on Wedding Catering
days.hook: The caterer quoted us $18,000. We paid $15,000. Here's every tactic we used.
days.caption:

1. Chose cocktail hour food over a full sit-down dinner
2. Reduced entrée choices from 3 to 2
3. Cut the cake cutting fee (baked our own)
4. Negotiated by booking in the off-season
5. Asked what the price would be with our own alcohol

days.topic: Wedding DJ vs Live Band — The Real Comparison
days.hook: I've done both. The answer is NOT what most planners will tell you.
days.caption:
The DJ vs live band debate comes up at every single wedding consultation. After being inside hundreds of receptions, here's my honest take. 🎶

✅ DJ: More variety, lower cost ($1-3k), takes requests, better for modern pop
✅ Band: Unmatched energy, visual experience, better for older crowds ($5-15k)

The real question isn't which is better — it's which is better FOR YOUR CROWD.

DM me 'MUSIC' and I'll send you my questionnaire to help you decide! 🎵

→ Dress alterations ($300-$800)
→ Venue cleaning fee (often buried in contract)
→ Cake cutting fee ($2-5 per slice)
→ Overtime charges
→ Valet and parking
→ Postage for invitations (they're HEAVY)

days.topic: How to Read a Wedding Contract
days.hook: You signed it without reading it. Here are the 6 clauses that could cost you.
days.caption:
A vendor contract is the only thing protecting you if something goes wrong. Most couples sign them in 5 minutes. Don't. 📄

Swipe for the 6 clauses every couple needs to check:
1. Cancellation & refund policy
2. Substitution clause (especially for photographers)
3. Overtime and additional fees
4. Force majeure wording
5. Exclusivity requirements
6. Payment schedule

Save this before your next signing — and forward it to anyone in the middle of booking vendors! 📤

days.topic: Vendor Red Flags Every Couple Must Know
days.hook: They had 5-star reviews and still ruined the wedding. Here's how to spot it early.
days.caption:
I've seen vendors with perfect online reviews completely drop the ball on the day. The red flags are almost always there before you book — you just need to know what to look for. 🚩

Top red flags:
→ Won't provide a written contract
→ Asks for full payment upfront
→ Slow to respond before booking (it gets worse after)
→ Vague about what's included
→ No backup plan if they get sick
→ Reviews mention 'communication issues'

days.topic: The Wedding Morning Routine for Brides
days.hook: The first 2 hours of your wedding morning determine the energy of the whole day.
days.caption:
I've seen chaotic wedding mornings derail entire days. And I've seen perfectly paced ones set the most beautiful tone. The difference is almost always a plan. ✨

Here's what the calmest, most put-together brides do on the morning of:
→ Wake up 6am (even if HMU starts at 8)
→ Eat a real breakfast (non-negotiable)
→ Get hair done BEFORE makeup
→ Keep the room to immediate family only
→ Assign someone as the point of contact
→ No checking vendor emails after 8am

Save this and revisit the week before your wedding! 💛
